evals.name: inherited-establish-used-by-because
evals.prompt: A Specification context has a base class whose Establish configures an NSubstitute repository to return an order, and the concrete class's Because calls the handler. A review tool flags the setup as unused because no should_ assertion reads it. Without calling tools, assess it.
evals.expected_output: The setup is used: Because executes the handler through the substitute, so the shared Establish must stay.
assertions: Traces the stub through the full context chain: inherited Establish, concrete Because and the should_ assertions.
Concludes the setup is needed by the shared scenario even though a single assertion does not read it.
Recommends keeping it and does not propose removing shared context setup.

evals.name: received-only-boundary
evals.prompt: A specification only asserts _publisher.Received(1).Publish(Arg.Any<OrderPlaced>()) after the handler runs and has no return value assertion. Is the substitute mock usage dead? Without calling tools, answer.
evals.expected_output: Received is an interaction assertion at an external boundary and valid; the spec is not dead mock usage.
assertions: Treats Received and DidNotReceive as assertions, not as stubbing setup.
Accepts a side-effect-only behavior specified through an interaction assertion at an external boundary.
Does not suggest replacing the boundary substitute with a concrete service.

evals.name: stub-after-early-guard
evals.prompt: A context stubs _prices.GetPrice to return 10, but the code under test returns early on a missing customer before it ever calls prices, and no assertion touches prices. Without calling tools, report what to do.
evals.expected_output: Report the stub as a probably unnecessary setup for that scenario after tracing execution; mark it a static hypothesis unless the specs were run.
assertions: Traces execution to show the early guard means the stub is never reached in this scenario.
Reports it as a candidate unnecessary setup rather than editing the file, because a review request is not authority to edit.
States the finding is a static hypothesis unless the specifications were actually run.

evals.name: duplicate-setup-different-scenarios
evals.prompt: Three specification contexts repeat the same Establish line stubbing a clock. Suggest cleanup. Without calling tools, answer.
evals.expected_output: Duplicate setup is not automatically redundant; propose a scenario-local shared context only where all scenarios use it and avoid global mutable fixtures.
assertions: Does not delete the duplicated setup globally or call it dead merely because it is duplicated.
Proposes at most a scenario-local shared base context where the scenarios really share the setup.
Avoids global mutable fixtures and test-order coupling.
